issues.legal_issue: A debtor co-sharer’s share of compensation for jointly held property cannot be paid to that co-sharer before the creditor co-sharers’ money claim is satisfied when the parties’ compromise decree makes the debtor co-sharer entitled only to the surplus.
material_facts: A compromise decree in a partition and rendition-of-accounts suit recorded that certain co-sharers owed money to the other co-sharers for amounts withdrawn from joint family funds.

The compromise decree provided that the debtor co-sharers could receive from compensation for acquired joint property only the surplus remaining after payment of the amount due to the creditor co-sharers.
Compensation was paid for some of the jointly held properties, and the creditor co-sharers’ money claim had not first been satisfied in full.
The trial court directed payment of the debtor co-sharers’ share of the compensation, and the High Court affirmed that order on revision.
issues.conclusion: The order directing payment to the debtor co-sharers was set aside because payment before satisfaction of the creditor co-sharers’ claim contravened the compromise decree. The amount attributable to the debtor co-sharers’ share was directed to be placed in a fixed deposit, without preventing payment to the creditor co-sharers of their share of the compensation.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of the compromise decree govern distribution of the compensation. Under its clause dealing with compensation for jointly held property, debtor co-sharers are entitled only to the surplus after the creditor co-sharers’ claim has been paid. The Court relied on the terms of the compromise decree and cited no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.appeal_from_compensation_distribution_or: An appeal challenges an order distributing compensation for jointly held property in a partition and rendition-of-accounts suit.
predicates.joint_property_compensation_received: Compensation was received for property held jointly by the co-sharers.
predicates.creditor_money_claim_remains_unsatisfied: The creditor co-sharers’ money claim has not been satisfied in full.
predicates.compromise_limits_debtor_compensation_to: The parties’ compromise provides that debtor co-sharers may receive compensation only from the surplus remaining after payment of the creditor co-sharers’ claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns distribution of compensation in a partition suit, compensation has been received for jointly held property, the creditor claim remains unsatisfied, and the compromise limits the debtor co-sharers to the surplus, the debtor co-sharers may be paid only after that claim is satisfied.
